blocks.content: The game needs screens. A menu when it loads. A pause panel mid-game. A game over result at the end.

All three use the same approach. A semi-transparent box drawn on top of the canvas, with text inside it. The game is still visible underneath through the transparency, which gives it a clean layered feel.
The box is drawn like this:
Calling fill() then stroke() paints the background first, then draws the border on top. This helper is reused by all three overlays — consistent styling from one source of truth.
Overlays render after entities in draw():
Background first, then entities, then overlays. That layering order is fundamental to 2D games. Everything renders beneath the overlay, visible through the semi-transparent panel.
You will call drawOverlayBox as a helper from all three overlay methods. One source of truth means consistent styling across every screen without repeating yourself.
Next, you will look at how to draw text inside the box for the menu and pause screens.
